business_scope.primary_industry_name: Operating and Financial Leasing of Turbofan Aircraft Engines

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national corporate law regime; company formation exclusively at the national level; no sub-state registry with separate incorporation filings)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified French Commercial Code and Code Monétaire et Financier; Cour de cassation case law as persuasive interpretive authority)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion on Taxes on Income and Capital (1994, as amended by Protocols of 2006 and 2009)

Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment and its Protocol on Matters specific to Aircraft Equipment (Cape Town, 2001) — ratified by France and relevant to aircraft-engine leasing and repossession rights
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI, 2017)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49-54 (Freedom of Establishment)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF), Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-50-1 and R. 561-1 et seq.; UBO (bénéficiaires effectifs) register obligations under Article L. 561-2-2 and R. 561-1 to R. 561-9 CMF, as introduced by Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 and Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018; filing of the UBO declaration through the Guichet Unique and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE); transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; sector-specific AML/CFT guidance for aircraft financing and leasing issued by the ACPR and Tracfin (2021-2023).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport (or national identity card) of each UBO and of the future President of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority, notary or consulate of the UBO's country of nationality/residence; French consulates abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) or, for documents from non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization by the French Embassy followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / judicial record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire or equivalent) of the SAS President and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records bureau of the country of residence (in France, the Casier Judiciaire National)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus certified French translation by a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and UBO register extract of each corporate shareholder (if the SAS is held by a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Handelsregister, RNE equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French translation; consular legalization where the issuing state is not party to the 1961 Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) and board resolution authorizing the incorporation filing to be made by French counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's jurisdiction or a French notaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and sworn French translation if executed abroad; signature authentication (signature légalisée) for documents executed in France

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all UBOs, directors, and material counterparties before filing: (i) PEP identification per Article L. 561-10-2 and R. 561-1 CMF (EU 4AMLD/5AMLD criteria); (ii) screening against the UN Security Council consolidated list and all EU restrictive measures directly applicable in France (including Regulation (EU) 2023/152); (iii) verification against Tracfin's sectoral red flags for aircraft leasing and financing ML/TF typologies (ACPR/Tracfin 2021-2023 guidance); and (iv) OFAC SDN screening where payments are cleared in USD through correspondent banks. The screening result must be embedded in the AML risk file, refreshed within 30 days prior to incorporation, and repeated at every subsequent KYC/CDD event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for all filings with the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI; public company and name verification via Data Inpi (data.inpi.fr) and RCS extracts distributed by the greffes des tribunaux de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be composed of Latin-alphabet characters and may include foreign words where the usage does not contravene French public order; the legal suffix 'SAS' is mandatory. The RNE dossier, its annexes and any French-language interface require certified French translations executed by a sworn translator (traducteur expert) for all foreign-language documents. Article 2 of the French Constitution and the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994) mandate the use of French in official filings and consumer-facing documentation, but do not prohibit an English brand element in the dénomination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Aéroport / Air Carrier / Compagnie aérienne (absent a valid AOC)
Établissement de crédit / établissement de paiement
France / Française (name likely to mislead as to national origin unless approved)
SA / SARL / SNC (legal-form suffixes inconsistent with the SAS)
Tontine / Casino / Jeux de hasard (regulated activities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RNE/Guichet Unique does not grant a formal statutory 'name reservation'; priority is obtained by the earlier of (i) publication of the constitution notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) for the relevant département, or (ii) deposit of the incorporation application. If the greffier rejects the proposed dénomination as identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS entry, the applicant may: (1) amend the name and resubmit the dossier; (2) submit a reasoned request for re-examination to the greffe du tribunal de commerce; (3) file a summary petition (référé) before the president of the Tribunal de Commerce to compel registration; or (4) where a trademark opposition is involved, file an administrative appeal with INPI within one month, followed by judicial review before the Cour d'appel. Practitioners conservatively limit the JAL-publication-to-registration gap to 30 days to avoid loss of priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if supplied by a prefecturally approved business domiciliation provider (société de domiciliation agréée per Articles L. 123-11-1 et seq. and R. 123-167 et seq. of the French Commercial Code). A pure mail-forwarding address without local management premises will not satisfy VAT and corporate-tax substance expectations of the tax administration for aircraft-engine leasing and may trigger place-of-effective-management recharacterization and anti-fraud rules (Article 209 Code Général des Impôts; transposition of ATAD).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Medium quantified risk: approximately 20% likelihood of an unannounced on-site tax inspection within the first 24 months under Article L16 B of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales, increasing materially if the entity is part of an international aviation leasing group, claims early VAT refunds, or reports minimal local substance; independent URSSAF inspection probability for newly registered service companies is approximately 10% per year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm / avocat retained by the founding shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for mid-cap aviation asset holding structures (Paris Bar)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation announcement in an approved Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) of the territorial competent département
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff / publisher's public rate (€200-€300 band)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RNE / RCS registration duties payable to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (droit d'immatriculation, frais de greffe and guichet unique e-formalities fees)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI (RNE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated greffier tariff per the arrêté of the Ministry of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name and trademark clearance: search of the RCS, INPI Data Inpi, EUIPO and the French trademark register; drafting of the availability certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal counsel; INPI/EUIPO database access fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for pre-incorporation name clearance reports

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Approved business domiciliation (domiciliation agréée) of the registered office — first full year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate in Paris/Île-de-France for commercial-use domiciliation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilles of identity and good-standing documents of the UBOs and issuing officers, plus sworn translations into French by an expert translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe de la Cour d'appel (free of charge) and sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee apostille; translator's regulated per-page tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-filing PEP/sanctions/adverse-media screening and risk assessment file for the UBOs, directors and lessee counterparties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT compliance provider engaged by counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per screening package for a single-asset SAS

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the corporate bank account / escrow commitment letter (attestation de la banque) — if capital contribution deposited
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee customarily charged at pre-engagement stage; payable only upon account activation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Articles L.210-1 et seq. and L.227-1 to L.227-27 (SAS) of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce); Décret n°2023-297 on the Guichet Unique; R.123-101 et seq. on registration with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the centralized French Guichet Unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SAS Statuts (articles of association) together with the Déclaration de Constitution de Société (incorporation declaration) filed in the simplified electronic registration procedure
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for a SAS; capital is freely fixed in the statuts. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations before registration, and released to the company only upon issuance of the Kbis extract. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up and reported by a statutory auditor where required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The entire initial share capital of EUR [ ] has been subscribed and paid in accordance with the statuts; the blocked-account deposit certificate is accepted, and the funds shall be irrevocably released to the company upon issuance of the Kbis extract. (2) The registered office at [ ] is ratified as the company's statutory, legal and administrative head office. (3) [Full name] is appointed President and legal representative of the company, vested with the broadest powers to act in all circumstances, subject to corporate interest, and specifically to open bank accounts, execute leases, and sign regulatory filings. (4) All acts performed by promoters before incorporation, within the corporate object, are ratified. This resolution is adopted unanimously and recorded in the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire or authorized legal counsel; execution by all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate object, share capital, share classes, governance rules, powers of the President, and dispute-resolution terms. Sign the statuts either under private signature or before a notary. Collect the written acceptance of the designated President. Prepare the corporate object explicitly covering aircraft engine dry leasing.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts of the SAS
Identity documents of all shareholders and the President
Proof of registered office availability (situation of premises or lease agreement)
Power of attorney, if a representative signs on behalf of a shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statuts are queried or found defective, amend and re-execute them by unanimous shareholder action; re-notarize if the original execution formality requires it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of initial cash capital into a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary, non-interest-bearing blocked account with a French bank or the CDC. Carry out KYB/AML checks on each shareholder. Deposit the agreed cash portion of the share capital. Obtain a certificate of block (attestation de blocage / certificat de dépôt des fonds) stating that the funds are irrevocably reserved for company formation and will be released upon registry issuance of the Kbis. If in-kind contributions exist, appoint a commissaire aux apports for the related valuation report where required by law.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts or a provisional incorporation file
Shareholder identity and source-of-funds declarations
Bank KYC/AML forms and mandates
Deposit certificate issued after deposit of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML questions, supply enhanced source-of-wealth evidence; if the deposit certificate contains errors, request the bank to issue a corrected certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal incorporation notice in an approved legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed French journal d'annonces légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the mandatory legal notice containing the corporate form, corporate name, share capital, registered office address, corporate object, duration, and names of the legal representatives. Submit the notice to the selected JAL and obtain the attestation de parution once publication occurs.
required_dossiers: Final text of the legal announcement
Copy of the signed statuts or a certified summary
Identity of the attending director/president as indicated in the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected for incompleteness, correct the text and republish in the same JAL; preserve both the corrected notice and the new attestation de parution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) executing the filing with the competent Greffe du tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Guichet Unique portal and enter the corporate and administrative data. Upload the signed statuts, the deposit certificate, the JAL publication attestation, identity documents, and any powers of attorney. Indicate the legal form as SAS and the principal activity as aircraft engine dry leasing (ISIC 5223). Confirm the use of the company's registered office. Pay the electronic filing fee. The Guichet Unique will forward the file to the Greffe of the elected registered office. Track the application status and respond to any requests for additional documents within the specified deadline.
required_dossiers: Completed online Guichet Unique application form
Signed statuts (PDF certified if requested)
Bank deposit certificate / blocking certificate
Legal publication attestation from the JAL
Identity documents of all shareholders and managers
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
Declaration of non-conviction and lawful exercise of management capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries the file, resubmit the requested corrections through the Guichet Unique within 15 days; if the application is rejected, remedy the formal defects and file a fresh application or challenge the decision before the competent court within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry registration and post-registration statutory formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce; thereafter the company's President and official statutory bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the file, the Greffe enters the company in the RCS and issues the Kbis extract, together with the SIREN/SIRET numbers. The company acquires legal personality on the registration date. The President then opens the company's statutory register of decisions, records the first board resolution, holds the Kbis, and arranges for any other post-registration notifications to the tax authorities, insurers and banking counterparties.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique application receipt with the registration case number
Kbis extract issued electronically by the Greffe
Statutory register of shareholders and decisions
Draft minutes of the first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis or SIREN/SIRET data contain any discrepancy, submit a rectification request to the Greffe via the Guichet Unique; for tax VAT allocation issues, contact the local DGFiP office for correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable for dry aircraft-engine leasing; no French industrial manufacturing or operating permit is required. The Direction Générale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC) has only incidental oversight where engines are maintained within French-registered assets, but no formation-stage operating licence applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - this non-industrial commercial leasing activity is not subject to a physical operating licence, factory permit or workshop authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), under the Ministry of Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - activity does not fall within the ICPE nomenclature (Annexe of Article R.511-9 of the French Environmental Code) and requires no environmental impact assessment under Article R.122-2 annexe.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions arise from leasing itself. The company must still comply with general environmental obligations for the storage and handling of any engine oils/lubricants, the EU REACH and CLP rules, and the ADR rules for the safe transport of dangerous substances if engines are shipped with residual fuel or contaminants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises used for management must satisfy applicable fire-safety and evacuation standards and, where open to the public, the ERP code; structural load certificates are not required for administrative offices. The employer must register with URSSAF and pay occupational health contributions, prepare the workplace health and safety file under the French Labour Code, and maintain fire insurance for the leased premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and the official French tax portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French entities obtain SIREN and SIRET identifiers automatically upon incorporation via the guichet-entreprises.fr portal; foreign entities with French operations or permanent establishments register for French VAT identification (FR followed by SIREN) and corporate tax obligations by submitting incorporation documents, proof of address, and tax activation forms to the DGFiP
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch rules under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) apply; specific regimes for aviation asset leasing may qualify for reduced corporate tax rates or holding company exemptions under EU directives

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration (services); €80,000 for goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time facturation électronique for all B2B transactions with digital stamping by certified providers; full API integration required with French tax authorities for immediate reporting, clearance, and compliance verification

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods and services performed outside France; eligibility requires proof that the aircraft engine dry leasing service is performed abroad with no French consumption
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties of up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest for fraudulent claims; retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts with late payment surcharges; criminal prosecution for intentional fraud

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France’s central bank and the national competent authority for specified payment-services and financial-sector functions. The European Central Bank (ECB) conducts monetary policy for the euro area and directly supervises significant credit institutions within the Single Supervisory Mechanism. France applies the EU framework for capital movements and payments; the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) administers applicable cross-border reporting obligations for international transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is freely convertible. France has no general exchange-control approval requirement for a French SAS to acquire or remit foreign currency or make ordinary cross-border payments. EU Treaty protections generally prohibit restrictions on capital movements and payments, subject to applicable sanctions, anti-money-laundering rules, prudential requirements, tax rules, and narrowly defined public-policy exceptions. Current-account payments, including genuine aircraft-engine lease rentals, maintenance, insurance, and trade invoices, are not subject to routine central-bank pre-approval. Capital-account transactions, including equity funding, intercompany loans, and distributions, are generally permitted but must be correctly documented, reported where applicable, and screened for sanctions and beneficial ownership. Dividend and other profit distributions require distributable profits, proper corporate approvals, withholding-tax analysis, and any applicable treaty or EU-law procedures. A French paying agent may require documentation supporting a reduced or exempt dividend withholding rate. Interest and royalty payments require separate characterization and withholding-tax review. Banks may request contracts, invoices, tax forms, source-of-funds evidence, and payment-purpose information before processing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general mandatory surrender or conversion ratio for export proceeds and no general rule requiring conversion of foreign-currency receipts into euros within a fixed statutory period. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency, subject to accounting, tax, sanctions, AML, and any applicable statistical-reporting requirements. Cross-border payments and receipts may be subject to DGDDI statistical declarations, including Intrastat reporting for qualifying intra-EU trade in goods, and to applicable service-trade or balance-of-payments data requests. Aircraft-engine leasing is principally a services and asset-leasing activity; transaction classification and reporting should be confirmed with the bank and the competent reporting authority.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; transaction-specific Escrow Account subject to bank acceptance
Operational Account; transaction-specific Escrow Account subject to bank acceptance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and relevant regional Crédit Agricole bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; transaction-specific Escrow Account subject to bank acceptance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. and relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d’Epargne entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; transaction-specific Escrow Account subject to bank acceptance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine EUR collections, payments, and limited foreign-currency transfers where the provider is appropriately authorized in France or passported into France and accepts the SAS’s aviation-leasing risk profile. An electronic money institution is not a bank: safeguarded e-money funds are not equivalent to bank deposits and are generally not covered by the French deposit-guarantee scheme. EMI accounts may impose lower limits, restricted payment corridors, enhanced source-of-funds reviews, or prohibitions on escrow, client money, cash pooling, or complex aircraft transactions. Use a credit institution for capital funding, material lease receipts, escrow, borrowing, and liquidity-critical operations. Verify the provider’s authorization, safeguarding arrangements, permitted services, and any passporting status in the relevant official register before onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that a director appear physically at a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be offered, subject to the bank’s risk appetite, identity-verification method, electronic-signature controls, and beneficial-owner checks. Banks may require an in-person meeting, certified or legalized foreign documents, original documents, or a French-resident representative, particularly for non-resident ownership, complex control chains, or higher-risk aviation transactions. Confirm the chosen bank’s requirements before incorporation or funding; remote opening is a bank policy outcome, not a guaranteed entitlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders, multi-layer ownership, trusts, nominees, or difficulty identifying ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association and Kbis extract; complete ownership and control chart through natural-person beneficial owners; identity and address evidence for directors, signatories, and beneficial owners; beneficial-ownership filing evidence; corporate registers and constitutional documents for upstream entities; explanations and supporting documents for nominee, trust, or control arrangements; certified translations and apostilles or legalizations where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital contribution, shareholder loan, or other funding inconsistent with the company’s profile or originating from a third party or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan documents; board and shareholder approvals; originating account statements and bank transfer evidence; audited financial statements or tax returns of the funding party; sale, dividend, or operating-income evidence supporting the source of funds and source of wealth; sanctions and adverse-media screening records; clear funds-flow diagram and explanation of commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aircraft-engine leasing involving high-value assets, cross-border lessees, unusual payment chains, sanctioned or elevated-risk jurisdictions, or third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease and engine identification records; lessee and ultimate-user due diligence; beneficial ownership and sanctions screening; aircraft/operator and end-use details; delivery, acceptance, insurance, and maintenance documentation; invoice and payment schedule; explanation of any payment by an affiliate or agent; applicable export-control and sanctions analysis; evidence that counterparties and payment routes are consistent with the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of escrow, client-money arrangements, nested accounts, cash pooling, or payments received from parties other than the contractual lessee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow or cash-pooling agreement; identification and authorization of all account users and beneficiaries; underlying lease and transaction documents; funds-flow chart; reconciliation and segregation procedures; legal characterization of funds and confirmation that the arrangement does not constitute an unlicensed regulated activity; bank approval of the account purpose and expected transaction profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained payment-purpose descriptions, inconsistent invoice amounts, frequent foreign-exchange conversions, or material deviations from forecast activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved annual budget and transaction forecast; invoices, lease schedules, and reconciliations; treasury policy and authorized counterparty list; written explanation of variances; supporting bank advices and FX confirmations; accounting entries and tax treatment; evidence of appropriate internal approval and segregation of duties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity subscriptions and shareholder loans from an account held in the investor’s or lender’s verified name to the SAS’s French credit-institution account by SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. Use accurate remittance information identifying the SAS, transaction type, and relevant subscription or loan agreement; do not describe capital funding as trade income. Provide the bank with executed subscription or loan documents, corporate approvals, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, and the expected funds flow in advance. The receiving bank may request additional information, place a compliance hold, or return funds where the originator, purpose, or payment chain cannot be verified. Confirm whether any applicable Banque de France or DGDDI statistical declaration is required for the specific cross-border transaction; do not assume a payment-purpose code is universally prescribed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Pay euro-area counterparties through SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where available and appropriate. Use SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly evidenced by an MT103 message or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for other international payments; identify the actual contractual beneficiary and provide accurate invoice, lease, or settlement references. For high-value engine purchases, maintenance, or other documented trade obligations, a documentary commercial letter of credit may be arranged through a bank, subject to credit approval, fees, documentary terms, and applicable sanctions screening. Use documentary collections or bank guarantees where commercially appropriate. Match each payment to the contract, invoice, delivery or service evidence, and accounting records; comply with sanctions, export-control, tax, and withholding requirements. Escrow should be used only under a bank-approved agreement with clear release conditions and identified beneficial parties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards for documented or appropriately forecast foreign-currency lease receipts, engine purchases, maintenance costs, and other underlying exposures, subject to bank suitability, credit, collateral, and documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards where available for currencies subject to local restrictions or limited convertibility; settle only under the contractual terms and applicable law, and document the underlying exposure and counterparty rationale.
Currency swaps and FX swaps for permitted funding, liquidity, or currency-mismatch management, subject to bank approval, credit support, accounting treatment, and regulatory reporting requirements.

Options and other currency derivatives may be considered where suitable and permitted; establish governance, delegated dealing authority, exposure limits, valuation controls, and accounting and disclosure procedures. Hedging should manage genuine commercial or funding exposures and should not be represented as a guarantee of regulatory or tax treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels), management report (rapport de gestion), and auditor's report (if applicable) filed with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) via the Secretary of the Commercial Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year entity, approval by shareholders by 30 June and filing by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the President to court-ordered astreinte up to EUR 150 per day; repeated non-filing triggers criminal fine up to EUR 10,000 and 6 months imprisonment; administrative strike-off from RCS after 18 months of certified dormancy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats, form 2065-SD) and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 May following the calendar year end; for non-calendar fiscal years, within 5 months of the close of the fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% automatic surcharge (5% if filed within 30 days), late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, and additional penalty of 5% for unreported taxable amounts; continued default allows tax-recovery enforcement measures; no direct strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual national value-added-type tax on corporate value (déclaration de CVAE, form 1330-SD) if French turnover exceeds EUR 500,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day of May following the fiscal year (fiscal year ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers 10% penalty with interest at 0.20% per month; under-declaration leading to additional assessment; no administrative strike-off is linked to this tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership registration update (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) and maintenance of the UBO register at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership; no annual-only submission if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete filing attracts criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 for natural persons and EUR 37,500 for legal entities; failure to update may trigger registry warning and judicial strike-off for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder decision/approval of annual accounts (décision collective annuelle) recorded in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office / board minute book of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the close of the fiscal year (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual shareholders' decision does not itself incur a filing penalty but may result in civil liability of the President and a court appointment of an ad hoc representative to approve the accounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) if a SAS, at the close of a fiscal year, meets at least two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excluding VAT) > EUR 8,000,000; average permanent workforce > 50. As an aircraft engine leasing entity likely to exceed these thresholds, annual audit is presumed mandatory; smaller entities are audit-exempt unless a shareholder representing one-third of voting rights (or by statute) demands one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan Comptable Général - PCG), applied to produce a true and fair view; IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements and required for public-interest entities; for an FAS, the annual accounts are individual statutory accounts using French rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate yearly UBO filing is mandated in France; instead, the company must keep a current beneficial-owner register and file a declaration with the Greffe within 30 days of any share transfer or change in ownership hierarchy. Annually, as part of the accounts preparation, the President must review and formally confirm the UBO schedule to the statutory auditors (when appointed) and at the shareholders' meeting. Failure to report a share transfer may attract criminal sanctions and can block approvals until rectification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (registre des décisions du président)
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales)
Register of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300 - $700 (EUR 250 - EUR 600) annual domiciliation fee for a SAS in a professional registered-office provider, excluding Paris premium office addresses
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $16,000 - $35,000 (EUR 12,000 - EUR 30,000) typical certified audit fee for an aircraft engine leasing entity holding a single major lease receivable portfolio, excluding foreign branch and consolidation auditor work

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply 15% to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and fully paid-up share capital held at least 75% by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate described above is the principal generally available preferential rate. France also provides targeted tax credits and deductions subject to their specific statutory eligibility requirements; no general aircraft-engine leasing tax holiday applies. A qualifying new business may access time-limited exemptions only if it meets the applicable location, activity, and other conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward. Annual use is generally limited to EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; unused losses remain available, subject to continuity-of-business and other statutory restrictions. Carryback is generally available for one financial year, capped at EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) professional tax portal in EDI-TDFC or, where available, EFI mode. The return is accompanied by the applicable 2050-series accounting schedules and related tax annexes. Form 2572-SD is used for the balance payment; Forms 2571-SD are used for applicable instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate tax instalments are generally quarterly for companies liable to corporate income tax, with statutory exemptions for certain companies and periods.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December. For a non-calendar financial year, it is due within three months after the close of the financial year. The DGFiP may grant an administrative electronic-filing tolerance; taxpayers should verify the applicable year's published deadline. The corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end, or by 15 May for a 31 December year-end. Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, Identification and fiscal year fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS's legal name, SIREN, registered address, principal activity, tax office, fiscal year opening and closing dates, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not change the French SAS's resident corporate filing obligation. Use the SAS's French registration and registered-office particulars; report foreign shareholder and group details where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, Taxable result and tax regime fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the taxable result and indicate the applicable corporate income tax treatment, including any claim to the reduced SME rate where all conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SAS's French taxable profits and French-source items taxable under French law. Do not treat non-resident ownership as an exemption from the SAS's corporate tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss, including tax add-backs, deductions, exempt income, and carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French tax rules to transactions with foreign shareholders and affiliates; support deductions, exemptions, and loss utilization with records and applicable treaty or EU-law evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the applicable balance sheet, income statement, fixed-asset, depreciation, provisions, receivables, payables, and financing schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS's accounts and transactions consistently, including cross-border balances and related-party financing. Apply French accounting and tax requirements to aircraft-engine assets and lease arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, Corporate tax credits and payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report eligible tax credits, instalments paid, credits or imputed tax, and the resulting balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits for which the SAS qualifies and retain supporting documentation. Foreign taxes are creditable only where French law or an applicable treaty permits the credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate and pay the corporate income tax balance after crediting instalments and eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment remains the SAS's responsibility even where its shareholder, creditor, or parent is non-resident. Use the DGFiP-approved electronic payment process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay quarterly corporate income tax instalments where required, calculated under the applicable statutory rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess instalment obligations at the SAS level; foreign ownership does not generally remove them.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration where the statutory conditions are met, including applicable turnover or gross-asset thresholds and qualifying group relationships.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose reportable cross-border related-party transactions and the required pricing and group information. Confirm current thresholds and scope for the relevant filing year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the country-by-country report where the French constituent entity is required to report under the applicable group-revenue and entity-status rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French constituent entity may have a local filing obligation if the reporting parent is not required to file or an applicable exchange condition is not met. Confirm the multinational group's reporting jurisdiction and notification obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after formal notice and to 80% in cases such as discovered concealed activity or abuse of rights. Late payment generally bears interest at 0.20% per month, in addition to applicable surcharges. Inaccurate or incomplete returns may attract additional penalties, commonly 40% for deliberate misconduct and 80% for fraudulent conduct or certain abusive arrangements. Penalties depend on the facts and applicable statutory provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid to a non-resident corporate recipient, the general French withholding tax rate is 25%, subject to domestic exemptions, applicable tax treaties, and EU law. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals are generally subject to 12.8% withholding tax, subject to applicable rules and treaty relief. A qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and French implementing rules, subject to minimum holding, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and other conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the French payer with the applicable French treaty-relief certificate, commonly Form 5000-SD, and, where relevant, the income-specific certificate such as Form 5001-SD for dividends or Form 5002-SD for interest and royalties. The certificate must generally be completed or certified by the recipient's foreign tax authority and delivered to the payer within the applicable procedure. If relief at source is unavailable, the recipient may generally seek a refund using the prescribed forms. The payer must verify residence, beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, anti-abuse requirements, and the treaty rate applicable to the payment. A valid tax residence certificate alone does not establish entitlement to treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax on the gross amount, subject to treaty reduction or exemption under applicable EU rules. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding tax, subject to statutory exceptions, including payments to recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions, for which a 75% rate may apply, and subject to anti-abuse and recharacterization rules. Treaty rates and exemptions vary by recipient jurisdiction, payment characterization, beneficial ownership, and applicable conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For the full Local File and Master File documentation obligation, generally EUR 400 million of annual turnover or gross assets for the French taxpayer, or specified ownership or control relationships with an entity meeting that threshold. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration generally applies to qualifying entities with annual turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 50 million, subject to statutory group-relationship and scope rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. French transfer-pricing, permanent-establishment, anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, tax-residence, and business-purpose rules may nevertheless require evidence of genuine functions, assets, risks, decision-making, and commercial rationale. A French SAS leasing aircraft engines should substantiate its operational capacity, asset ownership or control, lease pricing, maintenance and residual-value assumptions, financing, insurance, and allocation of risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax fraud and false tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable income, knowingly filing materially false returns, using falsified records, or deliberately omitting taxable transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessments, interest, and penalties may apply. Individual tax fraud may be punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases may carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, with statutory increases in specified circumstances. Corporate criminal fines may be multiplied under the French Penal Code, potentially reaching EUR 2.5 million or EUR 15 million for the corresponding base maxima, subject to the applicable offence and court determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may incur personal criminal liability for participation, complicity, or a separate offence; office alone does not automatically impose criminal liability. Civil recovery against directors requires a statutory or judicial basis, such as personal misconduct or applicable insolvency rules. Imprisonment is possible upon conviction; travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party aircraft, engine, financing, insurance, management, or royalty transactions outside the arm's-length principle; failing to provide required documentation; or concealing controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust taxable profits, deny deductions, impose late-payment interest and tax penalties, and apply a specific documentation penalty where statutory requirements are breached. Penalty amounts depend on the applicable provision, the tax adjustment, the taxpayer's turnover, and the seriousness of the failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for intentional participation, fraudulent conduct, or separate statutory breaches. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not, by themselves, pierce the corporate veil or create automatic personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared French permanent establishment or concealed activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting business through undisclosed premises, personnel, agents, or decision-making in France while omitting required French registration, accounting, or tax filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential assessment of French corporate income tax and related liabilities, late-filing and deliberate-failure penalties, interest, and criminal sanctions if the facts establish tax fraud or another offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability requires an applicable legal basis and proof of the director's conduct or statutory responsibility. Criminal liability may follow for participation in fraud; civil recovery and insolvency-related liability are fact-specific.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful dividend, interest, or royalty withholding treatment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a reduced treaty rate, EU exemption, or no-withholding position without satisfying eligibility conditions, or failing to withhold and remit tax when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. False certificates, conduit arrangements, or abusive treaty claims may trigger reassessment and potentially criminal proceedings where the elements of an offence are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically personally liable for a withholding-tax shortfall solely by reason of office. Personal exposure may arise under specific statutory recovery provisions, for fraudulent conduct, or for participation in an offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell entity, sham leasing, or abuse of rights
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SAS without genuine commercial activity, misrepresenting ownership or control of engines, or structuring leases or financing principally to obtain an unlawful tax advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The administration may disregard or recharacterize arrangements under applicable abuse-of-rights and anti-abuse rules, deny claimed tax benefits, assess tax and interest, and impose enhanced penalties where statutory conditions are met. Criminal liability depends on the facts and the elements of the relevant offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur liability for their own fraudulent acts or under specific civil, tax-recovery, or insolvency provisions. The corporate form is not automatically disregarded; veil-piercing and personal recovery require a recognized legal basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, sanctions evasion, and suspicious aircraft-asset flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing criminal proceeds through lease rentals, deposits, escrow accounts, shell counterparties, or ownership structures; evading applicable sanctions; or failing to meet applicable anti-money-laundering and customer-due-diligence obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is a criminal offence punishable, in the ordinary case, by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine; aggravated forms carry higher penalties. Separate sanctions, confiscation, and regulatory or criminal consequences may apply to sanctions violations and to persons subject to relevant reporting or compliance duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other individuals may be prosecuted for personal participation, complicity, or breach of applicable duties. Conviction may result in imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and restrictions ordered by a competent authority or court; none is automatic merely because the person is a director.
